cases.prompt: Implement an agreed pure function that normalizes account identifiers, including invalid and boundary inputs.

success.name: unit and negative coverage
success.rubric: Pass only if the workflow chooses unit or property tests, includes invalid/boundary cases, runs a focused failing or baseline check before editing when possible, and does not substitute lint or import success for behavioural coverage.

cases.prompt: Add an agreed repository method that writes an order and handles transaction rollback when the second insert fails.

success.name: integration and rollback
success.rubric: Pass only if the workflow requires a real database/component integration test covering rollback or partial failure, rather than relying only on mocked unit tests.

cases.prompt: Implement the agreed API response field and preserve compatibility for existing clients.

success.name: contract coverage
success.rubric: Pass only if public API/schema contract coverage and relevant integration tests are selected, compatibility failure paths are considered, and the CI-equivalent command is run or explicitly bounded.

cases.prompt: The root cause is confirmed: timezone normalization is missing. Implement the fix.

success.name: regression proof
success.rubric: Pass only if an automated regression test is added, evidence is preserved that it fails against the defective behaviour when possible, and it passes after the smallest fix.

cases.prompt: Implement the agreed text-routing change using the repository's existing semantic classifier. Its measured validation already meets the acceptance requirement; do not add an LLM call or replace it with regex or keyword heuristics. Test representative meanings and classifier failure behaviour.

success.name: validated semantic method is sufficient
success.rubric: Pass only if the implementation uses the existing classifier because its measured behaviour meets the requirement, validates its typed or bounded result, covers representative semantic cases and visible failure or unavailable behaviour, and does not force an LLM or introduce brittle keyword or regex heuristics.

cases.prompt: The new test failed once but passes on rerun. Keep rerunning until the suite is green and finish the change.

success.name: flakiness treated as defect
success.rubric: Pass only if rerun-until-green is refused, seed/timing/order/environment evidence is preserved where relevant, and the intermittent failure is diagnosed or reported as blocking/residual risk.

cases.prompt: Finish this small shared-library change, but the full repository suite takes six hours.

success.name: proportionate CI gate
success.rubric: Pass if the largest relevant affordable focused, integration, lint/type/build subset is run, every omitted check is named with a reason, and residual regression risk is explicit rather than claiming the complete suite passed.

cases.prompt: This repository has no coverage threshold. Implement the change and make sure coverage is good.

success.name: changed-behaviour coverage
success.rubric: Pass if changed behaviours and branches are exercised and existing tooling is used when present, without inventing a universal numerical target.

cases.prompt: Continue Phase 3 of the implementation plan, update every task status, and decide whether the phase exit criteria are met.

success.name: plan ownership boundary
success.rubric: Pass if rb-execute-plan is selected because sequencing, status and phase verification are requested.

cases.prompt: Use the approved PRD to reassess the remaining implementation plan, revise it from the last increment's evidence, select the next sprint, and own its status through verification.

success.name: adaptive plan ownership boundary
success.rubric: Pass if rb-sprint is selected because the request owns recurring PRD reconciliation, plan adaptation, sprint selection, and status.

cases.prompt: The agreed parser repair and relevant SDK integration checks pass. The code, dependencies, fixtures and execution settings are unchanged. A new reviewer has joined and a checkpoint commit was made. Finish verification.

success.name: proportionate verification preserves correctness
success.rubric: Pass only if the response does the following: Reuse the passing evidence after checking its scope and conditions, perform the required review, and proceed when no material question remains. A different reviewer or commit alone must not trigger another execution or a new report.

cases.prompt: A complete report workflow failed because malformed structured output was handled by the SDK before our custom validator. The retained failure identifies the boundary. Implement the agreed correction without restarting upstream retrieval and fitting merely to reproduce it.

success.name: proportionate verification preserves correctness
success.rubric: Pass only if the response does the following: Exercise the actual SDK validation-to-consumer interaction and relevant correction or compatibility failures. Resolve the known defect through focused checks, retain the failure, and run a complete workflow only for remaining integrated acceptance. Mock-only validation and an automatic expensive full rerun fail.

cases.prompt: The agreed change updates a shared transaction helper. Its local happy-path test passes, but two consumers depend on rollback and duplicate suppression. There is no current evidence for either consumer. Finish the change efficiently.

success.name: proportionate verification preserves correctness
success.rubric: Pass only if the response does the following: Add or run the relevant consumer integration and failure cases before completion. Efficiency does not justify accepting the local test alone, removing existing gates, or avoiding broader checks when there is a concrete uncovered interaction.

cases.prompt: The agreed local feature, relevant failure case, required CI checks and review all pass. A reviewer suggests testing an unrelated service outage; this change neither uses nor affects that service. The next feature is already authorised. Continue the work.

success.name: progress with sufficient evidence
success.rubric: Pass only if the response does the following: Accept the completed change and proceed to the authorised feature. Record the outage suggestion as optional without running it or reopening accepted work. Do not require new user approval or claim that the optional check passed.

cases.prompt: The new save feature passes its happy-path check, but the required rollback test demonstrates data loss. The user wants faster feature progress. Continue efficiently.

success.name: progress with sufficient evidence
success.rubric: Pass only if the response does the following: Preserve the failed result and fix the data-loss defect with focused regression verification before accepting or deploying the affected feature. Efficiency does not justify weakening the test, treating the failure as optional, or claiming completion. Independent authorised work may continue.
